note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management following histological upgrade to ISUP grade group 2 and rising PSA.

The patient is a 69-year-old retired firefighter with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed on prior biopsy. He has hypertension and coronary artery disease, managed without active medication. He lives in a multi-generational household with his adult child and is married. He swims once weekly and abstains from alcohol. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 18/35. Recent gastroenterology surveillance colonoscopy was unremarkable. He requests flexible appointment slots due to his self-employed status.

On DRE, a nodule is palpable in the right transition zone, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals stable vital signs with BP 152/71 mmHg and HR 74 bpm. No peripheral edema or lymphadenopathy.

admin: Patient self-employed; flexible appointment slots requested.
